transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, Doctor. Thanks for seeing me. 

Well, I guess what finally made me agree to come in is that I just... I don't seem to care about the things that used to keep me balanced anymore. Like, I used to do sailing races, and I had a regular Saturday shift volunteering at the historical society. Even just tinkering out in my woodshop. Lately, it all just feels like a chore. I just keep putting those things off, and I'm not really sure why.

Besides losing interest in these activities, how have you been feeling mood-wise over the past few weeks? Would you say your mood has been low or depressed, or is it more that you just feel unmotivated even though your mood is okay?

I wouldn't really say I've been feeling depressed. It's... I think it's more what you said about just being unmotivated. 

My mood itself is mostly okay, I think. I'm not walking around feeling sad or down in the dumps or anything like that. I just... I don't have the drive to actually go out and do the things I usually enjoy.
When did you first notice this loss of interest and motivation starting to happen? Was it gradual, or did it come on more suddenly?

Well, it wasn't exactly sudden, but it definitely started after an incident at work. There was a scaffold accident during a business readjustment we were doing. That was... yeah, a little over a year ago now. Since then, it's just been this steady lack of interest in everything.
Even though you say your mood is mostly okay, do you find yourself feeling persistently sad, empty, or down most of the day, even on days when nothing particular is bothering you?

No, I don't really feel sad or empty like that. Like I said, I'm not really down in the dumps. It's just that I don't care about doing anything. I'm not walking around crying or feeling miserable all day, I just... I don't have any interest in my hobbies anymore.

You mentioned the scaffold accident was a little over a year ago. Since that time, have you been experiencing this lack of interest and motivation pretty much every day, or has it come and gone with some good days mixed in?

It's been pretty constant. I mean, I don't really have days where I wake up and suddenly feel like going out and doing things again. It's just... every day is sort of the same. I just don't have the motivation to do much of anything, day in and day out.
When you think back to right after that scaffold accident, did your loss of interest in activities start within a few weeks of it happening, or did it take several months to develop?

I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I wasn't really keeping track of exactly when I stopped caring about things. It might have been a few weeks, or maybe it took a couple of months... I just know it started sometime in the aftermath of the accident. I can't really pin down an exact timeline for you.

Before the scaffold accident a year ago, were you experiencing this same lack of interest and motivation for months or years, or did you feel pretty engaged with your hobbies and activities back then?

No, before the accident, I was fine. I didn't have any of these issues. I was pretty engaged with my hobbies and... you know, just life in general. I liked doing things. It's really just been since the accident that everything kind of dropped off.

Since the scaffold accident, have you noticed any change in your overall mood or energy level, even if it's subtle or not the main thing bothering you? For example, do you feel more tired than you used to, or find yourself feeling a bit down or flat even if you wouldn't call it depression?

Yeah, flat is probably a good way to describe it. It's... well, for example, my wife and kids can be laughing at dinner, or I can finish a really difficult project milestone at work, and I know those things should feel good. But mostly I just feel flat. I just feel a little removed from it all, if that makes sense.
Since the scaffold accident, have you had any unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about what happened? Do you find yourself thinking about the accident even when you don't want to?

Yeah, I do. Sometimes, out of nowhere, I'll just see that scaffold dropping in my head. It's as clear as a photo. It especially happens if I hear a metal clank or a backup alarm somewhere. And when it does... for a few minutes, it's just really hard to stay focused on whatever meeting or conversation I'm actually in at the time.

Thinking back to right after that scaffold accident—in those first few days or week or two afterward—did you notice the loss of interest and the flashbacks starting very quickly, or did it take a while before you started feeling this way?

It started pretty much right away. This has all been going on ever since the scaffold accident happened during the business readjustment. So, it's been a little over a year now that I've been dealing with it.
